battle.name: 新西蘭土地戰爭
battle.theater: 南島塔斯曼灣懷勞河谷
battle.brief: 1845年6月，紐西蘭南島懷勞河口的殖民民兵與特拉帕拉哈率領的土阿聯軍因購地糾紛開火，揭開紐西蘭戰爭第二階段。卡面這件1840年法式雷管步槍正是同代技術：底火讓步槍在濕霧中照樣齊射，英軍得以在土牆外先用彈雨壓住毛利戰士，後來陶朗加與奧拉考的攻防也據此重排火炮與步槍的配比。

kit.name: 雷管步槍
kit.history: 雷管取代火燧之後，底火在霧裡也打得響。射程變長，隊形就散了。

countries: 紐西蘭土地戰爭自1843年英軍佔領科羅拉雷卡起，到1872年最後一役止，前後近三十年，通常分為旗桿戰爭、第二階段與1860年代起的第三階段三段。英方是1840年建檔的英屬紐西蘭殖民地，骨幹是由英國國會撥款維持的帝國部隊：陸軍方面投入過第50、第65、第96等團，第三階段再加上第18、第40、第43、第57團，以及懷卡托第一至第四團等殖民地團；另有皇家海軍陸戰隊、皇家炮兵（配備六磅、九磅、十二磅與二十四磅野戰炮及迫擊炮，1860年代中期開始裝備阿姆斯特朗後膛炮）、皇家工兵，以及由海軍陸戰隊與水手組成、配船上火炮的皇家海軍分遣隊。殖民地方面有奧克蘭、納爾遜、坎特伯雷與奧塔哥民兵、國防軍與後來的志願部隊，以及1863年後湧入懷卡托的定居者自組隊伍。毛利一方並非國家，而是聯盟與部族：納蒂托阿、納蒂勞卡瓦與陶阿蒂阿瓦在第一、二階段與英方對抗；納蒂豪與提托科瓦魯在北部堅持；1860年成立的毛利王運動以納蒂馬尼亞波、納蒂勞塔瓦等為主力，總督喬治·格雷把它定性為叛亂組織，戰爭因此帶上鎮壓內亂的性質。第三方則是保持中立的毛利人、效忠王室的部族首領，以及1870年代接替格雷的總督。
countriesEn: The New Zealand Wars ran from the British occupation of Kororareka in 1843 to the last campaign of 1872, close to thirty years in all, and are conventionally divided into three phases: the Flagstaff War, the second campaign, and the third campaign that began in the 1860s. On the British side stood the colony of New Zealand, established as a Crown colony in 1840, with an Imperial army paid for by the British parliament forming its backbone: on the land the campaigns involved the 50th, 65th and 96th Foot, and in the third phase the 18th, 40th, 43rd and 57th, together with colonial units such as the First to Fourth Waikato Regiments; besides these there were the Royal Marines, the Royal Artillery (with six-, nine-, twelve- and twenty-four-pounder field guns and mortars, and Armstrong breech-loading pieces from the mid-1860s), the Royal Engineers, and the naval brigades drawn from the Royal Navy, made up of marines and bluejackets with ship guns and, later, heavy Armstrong rifles. On the colonial side were the Auckland, Nelson, Canterbury and Otago militias, the fencibles, the volunteer force that came later, and the settler companies that poured into the Waikato after 1863. The Maori side was not a state but a set of alliances and iwi: Ngati Toa, Ngati Raukawa and Te Ati Awa faced the British in the first and second phases; Ngati Hau and Titokowaru held the north; the Maori King movement founded in 1860 drew its strength from Ngati Maniapoto, Ngati Rautawa and others, and because Governor George Grey declared the Kingitanga a rebellion, the war came to carry the character of a campaign of suppression. Third parties were the many iwi who stayed neutral or sided with the Crown, and the governors who took over from Grey in the 1870s.
people: 英方關鍵人物分三類：總督、戰場指揮官、還有授權與議決的人。喬治·格雷兩度出任總督（1845至1853年、1861至1868年），他既是對毛利土地承諾的談判者，也在1863年下令進攻懷卡托、1864年換下道格拉斯·卡梅倫改派納皮爾，是政策轉向的樞紐。北部兵事由亨利·德斯帕德中校指揮，第二階段先後由威廉·休姆上校、湯瑪士·普拉特接手，卡梅倫在1846年之後主持惠靈頓、懷拉帕與旺加努伊戰役，1863年再度被召回執掌懷卡托，1864年陶朗加之役的戰場指揮則由喬治·納皮爾少將接手；1868年之後由亞歷山大·邁克唐納與喬治·鮑恩總督接棒，1872年的最後一役由湯瑪士·麥克戴維特指揮。殖民地方面，懷勞之役的指揮是科隆納·威克菲爾德上校與亞瑟·威克菲爾德中尉。毛利方面的名字更長：特拉帕拉哈是第二階段的主要對手，特·朗吉海阿塔在惠靈頓一線一度令英軍最精銳的連隊覆沒；北部由霍內·赫克與特魯基·卡維蒂先後斬旗桿；提托科瓦魯帶著納蒂豪人的抵抗撐到1872年；提庫蒂與提·維蒂在1860年代流竄作戰；重建王國的維利·馬尼亞波托、維雷穆·塔懷奧、維雷穆·金吉與特·朗吉希維努伊，在奧拉考與提·蘭加一線扛住英軍主力。
peopleEn: The British figures fall into three kinds: governors, battlefield commanders, and the men who authorised and voted for the war. George Grey served twice as governor (1845-53 and 1861-68); he was at once the negotiator of the Crown's promises about Maori land and the man who in 1863 ordered the invasion of the Waikato and in 1864 replaced Douglas Cameron with Napier, and he is the hinge of the policy change. In the north the fighting was directed by Lieutenant-Colonel Henry Despard; in the second phase it passed in turn to Colonel William Hulme and then Thomas Pratt, and Douglas Cameron took over after 1846 for the Wellington, Wairarapa and Whanganui campaigns, was recalled to command the Waikato in 1863, and in 1864 the field command at Tauranga went to Major-General George Napier, with Alexander McDonnell and George Bowen following as governors and Thomas McDavitt directing the last campaign of 1872. On the colonial side the Wairau affair was commanded by Colonel Charles Wakefield and Captain Arthur Wakefield. The Maori names are longer still: Te Rauparaha was the chief opponent of the second phase, and Te Rangihaeata in the Wellington district destroyed the picket of one of the British Army's finest companies; in the north Hone Heke and Te Ruki Kawiti cut down the flagstaff in turn; Titokowaru carried Ngati Hau's resistance through to 1872; Te Kooti and Te Whiti campaigned in exile through the 1860s; and Rewi Maniapoto, Wiremu Tawhiao, Wiremu Kingi and Te Rangihiwinui held the main body of the British at Orakau and Te Ranga.
kits: 卡面這件1840年法國雷管步槍，是雷管技術世代的樣本：法國的雷管自1820年代起在歐陸推廣，1840年前後正是歐洲各國制式步槍交替的世代分界。它不是英軍在紐西蘭的制式槍，但英軍手中正是同代的東西——英軍步兵團裝備.54口徑雷管滑膛槍，即俗稱「褐色貝絲」的舊型換上雷管點火，近身則改用卡賓槍；1845年的第65、第50團與民兵使用的即是這類雷管槍，優點是不怕潮濕、單兵可自行裝填、一分鐘內能打出數十發齊射，也不必再在火藥盤上灑引火藥粉。1860年代中期英軍換上阿姆斯特朗後膛炮與馬丁尼—亨利式後膛槍，火力與精度再上一層。毛利一方則靠另一條路取得火器：從商船與私人貿易手中買進.54滑膛槍，1861至1862年間更成批購入美國內戰後輸出的「帕夫」連發槍，每分鐘可射八至十發，一度在射速上壓過英軍線列步兵；到1863至1864年英軍改用後膛槍與步槍散兵線，這個差距才被抹平。除火器外，決定戰局還有砲兵：六磅、九磅與二十四磅野戰炮、迫擊炮，以及海軍分遣隊裝備的六磅、十二磅、二十四磅船炮與四十磅、百一十磅阿姆斯特朗後膛速射炮，1864年奧拉考圍城時「艾斯克」號的百一十磅速射炮是英軍最重的一件火器。運輸靠沿海帆船與汽船的登陸點、駁船、駁運與馬匹，1863年遠征懷卡托時更得在沒有道路的內陸靠人力與馱馬搬運。
kitsEn: The French percussion rifle of 1840 on the card is a sample of the percussion generation of technology: percussion ignition spread across continental Europe from the 1820s, and around 1840 came the point at which the standard musket of every European army changed over. It was not the standard arm of the British Army in New Zealand, but what the British held belonged to the same generation: the .54 calibre percussion smoothbore musket, the India pattern, in effect the old Brown Bess with new ignition, with carbines for close work. The 65th and 50th Foot and the militia in 1845 used precisely such percussion guns, whose merits were that they did not mind damp, that a man could load his own cartridge, that a company could put several dozen rounds into the air in a minute, and that the priming powder no longer had to be sprinkled on the pan. In the mid-1860s the British changed to Armstrong breech-loading guns and the Martini-Henry breech-loader, gaining a further step in power and accuracy. The Maori took a different road to the same weapons: they bought .54 smoothbore muskets from merchants and private trade, and between 1861 and 1862 they bought in quantity the 'puffer' repeating rifles that American manufacturers were selling after the American Civil War, capable of eight to ten shots a minute, which for a time gave them a rate of fire that outstripped the British line infantry; only in 1863-64, when the British switched to the breech-loader and to rifle skirmishers, was that gap closed. Artillery mattered as much as muskets: six-, nine- and twenty-four-pounder field guns and mortars, the ship guns of the naval brigades at six-, twelve- and twenty-four-pounder, and forty- and one-hundred-and-ten-pounder Armstrong breech-loading rifles, the 110-pounder from HMS Esk being the heaviest piece in the British line during the siege of Orakau in 1864. Transport was by coastal sailing craft and steamship landings, by lighter and by horse, and the march into the Waikato in 1863 meant carrying everything by hand and on pack-horse across a country with no roads.
tactics: 英軍的戰術在三十年裡換了兩次。1840年代是線列加散兵的組合：步兵以連為單位排成密集橫隊，軍官一聲令下整連齊射，彈雨壓過去再上刺刀；攻毛利教坊時先用炮兵把牆頭犁一遍，再以縱隊接連突擊，1845年1月魯阿佩卡佩卡一役正是這種節奏的示範：炮兵整日轟擊毛利在教坊內挖出的塹壕與內壘，入夜後英軍摸黑推進，守軍在退路被截斷的情況下放棄教坊。1860年代起，英軍吸收毛利教坊的教訓，改為「以炮制坊」：先用海軍分遣隊與炮兵團的遠程炮火消耗，再以散兵線前進，步槍手利用土壘與彈坑逐步接近，最後由工兵開挖塹壕接近，突擊手才衝上牆頂。奧拉考圍城最能說明變化：毛利在教坊外挖了深溝，牆面以樹枝加固，婦孺與傷者退入內部塹壕，防守方以步槍和連發槍壓制英軍散兵線，英軍則靠百一十磅速射炮與迫擊炮轟擊缺口，最後仍要靠刺刀與炸藥攻破木柵。毛利方面則長期採取流動戰團的辦法，不把主力押在一座教坊上，用聯隊式的戰鬥群在內陸轉戰、夜襲、斷糧；瓦雷卡之役是在行軍縱隊中設伏，1863年之後王國軍大量騎馬，四十餘騎在英軍巡邏線之間快速打擊後方，使英軍不得不保留騎兵與流動分遣隊，1863年懷卡托河登陸與拉奇里里攻堅也是英軍把縱隊、器材、糧秣同時用船運到灘頭的結果。
tacticsEn: British tactics changed twice in thirty years. The 1840s combined line and skirmish: infantry stood in dense company fronts, the officer gave the word and the whole company fired, and the volley went over before the bayonets went forward; against a Maori pā the guns shelled the parapet first and the assault columns came on in succession, and the battle of Ruapekapeka in January 1845 is the model of that rhythm, with the artillery bombarding all day the trenches and inner ramparts the Maori had dug into the pā, the English creeping forward after dark, and the defenders abandoning the pā once their lines of retreat were cut. From the 1860s the British absorbed the lesson of the Maori pā and changed to the doctrine of killing the pā with artillery: long-range fire from the naval brigades and the field batteries first, then skirmishers advancing under cover of earthworks and shell holes, riflemen working forward by degrees, and finally the sappers digging a sap to within reach before the storming parties went over the top. The siege of Orakau shows the change best: the Maori dug a deep ditch outside the pā, strengthened the facing with timber, and moved the women, children and wounded into the inner trench, while the defenders held the British skirmishers down with rifles and repeating guns, and the British answered with the 110-pounder Armstrong and mortars, still having to break the timber palisade with the bayonet and explosives. The Maori in turn long kept to the warband that refused to be pinned to a single pā: fighting groups moved about the interior, struck at night and cut off supplies; Waireka was an ambush laid on a marching column; after 1863 the Kingitanga fielded a great many horses, and a band of several dozen riders struck at the British rear between patrols, forcing the British to keep cavalry and mobile detachments, and the landings on the Waikato river at Rangiriri were the outcome of a British plan to bring the column, its stores and its baggage ashore by water in a single movement.
data: 可核對的數字集中在幾個點上。時間軸：1843年3月11日英軍佔領科羅拉雷卡，3月14日旗桿被砍；1845年1月11日魯阿佩卡佩卡，1月22至23日恩加塔帕與奧哈瓦瓦伊，4月29日普克塔普；1845年6月11日懷勞之役；1846年4月29日大門教坊；1847年1月布爾科特農場與波里魯瓦，5月21日特·朗吉海阿塔教坊；1860年3月17日懷塔拉，3月28日瓦雷卡，1861年5月28日摩科普瓦伊提亞；1863年10月12日拉奇里里；1864年3月28日起奧拉考圍城，6月24日提·蘭加；1872年10月8日最後一役。懷勞之役英方損失有明確記錄：二十二人陣亡、六十一人受傷，毛利方面的數字各方說法不一。奧拉考圍城英軍損失一般記為十三人陣亡、三十九人受傷，另有十四人的說法。兵力方面，1863至1864年懷卡托戰役英軍投入約三千五百人，其中二千名帝國正規軍、一千餘名民兵與志願者以及五百名海軍分遣隊員；1864年陶朗加投入的英軍約一千八百人；毛利方面1864年在奧拉考一線約有七百至八百名戰士。人口對照：1861年紐西蘭歐洲人口約四萬八千人，毛利約三萬五千人。1862年前後政府放售給毛利約二千支卡賓槍與數百支手槍，連發槍是其中一部分。土地沒收方面，1865年《新西蘭戰爭法》之後，懷卡托被沒收的土地以百萬英畝計。
dataEn: The verifiable figures cluster around a few points. The timeline: 11 March 1843 the British occupied Kororareka, and on 14 March the flagstaff was cut down; 11 January 1845 Ruapekapeka, 22-23 January Ngatapa and Ohaeawai, 29 April Puketapu; 11 June 1845 the Wairau affair; 29 April 1846 the Gate pā; January 1847 Boulcott's Farm and the pā at Porirua, 21 May 1847 Te Rangihaeata's pā; 17 March 1860 Waitara, 28 March Waireka, 28 May 1861 Mokopawaitia; 12 October 1863 Rangiriri; from 28 March 1864 the siege of Orakau, and on 24 June Te Ranga; 8 October 1872 the last action. British losses at the Wairau are recorded clearly: twenty-two killed and sixty-one wounded, while the Maori figures are given differently by different sources. British losses at Orakau are generally recorded as thirteen killed and thirty-nine wounded, with some sources giving fourteen. On strength: the British put about three thousand five hundred men into the Waikato campaign of 1863-64, of whom two thousand were Imperial regulars, a little over a thousand were militia and volunteers, and five hundred were naval brigade; roughly eighteen hundred were committed at Tauranga in 1864; on the Maori side something between seven hundred and eight hundred fighters were engaged in the Orakau line in 1864. For population, the European population of New Zealand stood at about forty-eight thousand in 1861 and the Maori population at about thirty-five thousand. Around 1862 the government allowed the sale to the Maori of some two thousand carbines and several hundred pistols, and the repeating rifles were part of that number. On confiscation, after the New Zealand Wars Act of 1865, the land taken in the Waikato ran to a million acres and more.
cause: 戰爭的起因是土地，而土地問題在1840年《新西蘭條約》之後被英國視為已經解決。三份條約把原住民土地列為受保護的產權，並許諾在毛利人同意下出售土地；此後紐西蘭公司與定居者卻以低價在私下交易中大量收購，1840年代北部的教坊衝突正源於這種一邊賣、一邊駐軍的處境。1843年英軍佔領科羅拉雷卡並升起英國旗桿，被毛利人視為對條約承諾的挑釁，霍內·赫克與卡維蒂因此砍倒旗桿。1850年代，總督與各公司把大片待售地按一紙合約撥給移民；1860年3月17日，紐西蘭公司在總督主持下把懷塔拉地區約十萬英畝土地售與定居者，條件是毛利人放棄土地保有權，陶阿蒂阿瓦部族拒絕，答應的款項被扣留，懷塔拉的旗桿隨即被砍落，1860年代的戰爭由此爆發。第三階段更根本的原因，是喬治·格雷把毛利王的國度定性為叛亂組織，並在1863年決定以正規軍深入懷卡托、沒收土地，把毛利人的抵抗從條約糾紛改寫成叛亂鎮壓；英方同時在1860年代中期允許並協助毛利購買新式連發槍，等於在軍備上拉平對手，再以遠征方式尋求解決。
causeEn: The war began with land, and after 1840 the British regarded the land question as settled. The three Treaty of Waitangi documents listed native land as protected property and promised that land would be sold with Maori consent; the New Zealand Company and the settlers nonetheless bought up large tracts in cheap private transactions, and the pā conflicts of the 1840s in the north grew out of this situation of selling on one side and garrisoning on the other. In 1843 the British occupied Kororareka and raised the British flagstaff, which the Maori read as a challenge to the treaty's promises, and Hone Heke and Kawiti accordingly cut it down. Through the 1850s the governor and the companies allocated large blocks of surveyed land to immigrants on paper; on 17 March 1860 the New Plymouth Company, with the governor's assent, bought about a hundred thousand acres at Waitara on condition that the Maori renounce their title to it, Te Ati Awa refused, the purchase money was withheld, and the flagstaff at Waitara came down shortly afterwards, which was the flashpoint for the wars of the 1860s. The deeper cause of the third phase is that George Grey defined the Maori King's country as a rebel organisation and in 1863 resolved to send regular troops deep into the Waikato and confiscate land, rewriting Maori resistance from a dispute about the treaty into the suppression of a rebellion; at the same time, in the mid-1860s the British allowed and assisted the purchase of modern repeating rifles by the Maori, that is, they levelled the armament of their opponent before seeking a solution by invasion.
impact: 戰爭的後果由三條線構成。第一是土地與國家權力：毛利王國被判定為非法，1865年《新西蘭戰爭法》授權沒收叛亂部族的土地，懷卡托與塔拉納基先後有大片田產被沒收並改劃移民定居，英國在紐西蘭的主權由與毛利共享變成唯一最高權力，毛利土地所有權問題自此成為整個十九世紀紐西蘭政治的主線，1879年的土地購買條例與1890年代以後的土地法庭都源於此。第二是軍事技術的教訓：炮兵、散兵線與後膛槍把毛利經營了幾百年的教坊防禦徹底壓倒，但英軍每前進一哩都要自己修路，倉庫、柴薪與飼料全靠人力搬運，這使英方在1870年代之後從遠征鎮壓轉向設防管治。第三是人的去向：被捕的毛利領袖被流放或囚禁，沒收的土地留下叛亂地的名字，王國運動的傳承在流亡中延續，1865年後大批部族土地被劃為遷徙區，部族被迫分散居住，這是戰爭之後數十年毛利社會變動的源頭，也是二十世紀初毛利土地問題與文化復振的遠因。
impactEn: The consequences of the war run along three lines. The first is land and state power: the Maori King state was judged illegal, the New Zealand Wars Act of 1865 authorised the confiscation of the lands of rebel iwi, large areas in the Waikato and Taranaki were taken and redrawn as settler farms, and British sovereignty in New Zealand changed from something shared with the Maori into a single supreme authority; the question of Maori land title then became the main line of New Zealand politics for the whole of the nineteenth century, and both the land purchase of 1879 and the land courts of the 1890s grew out of it. The second is the lesson of military technology: artillery, skirmish lines and the breech-loading rifle crushed the pā that the Maori had been building for centuries, but every mile the British advanced they had to road it themselves, with stores, firewood and fodder all carried by hand, and this is what turned British policy, from the 1870s onward, from distant expedition and suppression towards garrisoned administration. The third is where the people went: captured Maori leaders were exiled or imprisoned, the confiscated lands carried the name of rebel land, the inheritance of the King movement was kept alive in exile, and after 1865 large areas of tribal land were turned into resettlement districts which dispersed the iwi; that is the origin of the social upheaval among the Maori in the decades after the war, and the distant cause of the land struggles and the cultural revival of the early twentieth century.
result: 打從1872年10月8日最後一役英軍攻入毛利聚落為止，新西蘭的土地戰爭以英方的完全勝利告一段落。1860年代之後的戰役已經沒有旗桿可砍，也沒有象徵可爭，剩下的是純粹的兵力與物資對比：英軍以團級部隊配合海軍分遣隊的炮火，逐個收拾王國的據點，1864年提·蘭加一役之後懷卡托戰線崩解，1868年東角與塔拉納基的戰役清除最後抵抗，1872年提·維蒂與魯阿·基納納在提阿瓦馬魯被捕，戰爭的立法期限亦隨之到期。戰術層面的結果最直觀：教坊從此退出現役，要塞由石砌炮台與常備軍取代，1876年特拉帕拉哈在流亡地病逝時，他所代表的部族勢力仍未被完全拆散。武器層面則是卡面那件雷管步槍所代表的世代完成了使命，它把齊射擺上射擊線，讓對面用泥土堆起來的防禦失去意義，之後的戰爭交給後膛炮、鐵路與更長的射程，紐西蘭也從此成為常備軍與殖民政府的試驗場。
resultEn: From the last action of 8 October 1872, when the British moved against the Maori settlements, the New Zealand Wars came to a close in complete British victory. After the 1860s there was no flagstaff left to cut and no symbol left to contest, only a plain comparison of men and materiel: regiments working with the fire of the naval brigades took the Kingitanga's positions one by one, the Waikato line came apart after Te Ranga in 1864, the campaigns in the East Cape and in Taranaki in 1868 cleared away the last resistance, and Te Whiti and Rua Kenana were taken at Te Awamaru in 1872, at which point the statutory life of the war ran out. The tactical result is the most plain: the pā went out of service and the fixed pā gave way to stone-built batteries and a permanent army, and when Te Rauparaha died in exile in 1876 the force he represented had still not been wholly broken up. At the level of weapons, the generation represented by the percussion rifle on the card had completed its task: it put the volley on the firing line and made the defence the Maori had piled up out of earth meaningless, and the wars after that were handed over to the breech-loader, the railway and greater range, while New Zealand itself became a testing ground for the permanent army and the colonial government.
